title: Presigned upload: the API grants permission, the bytes skip your servers
caption: Your service handles one small JSON request; the 2 GB of video goes straight to object storage.

messages.label: POST /uploads {clip.mp4, 2 GB}
messages.note: Auth, quota and file-type checks happen here, on a tiny request.

messages.label: insert video row (pending)
messages.note: The row owns the key videos/v_77/raw.mp4.

messages.label: presigned PUT URL (15 min)
messages.note: Signed for one operation on one key, with an expiry and optionally a size cap.

messages.label: PUT bytes (multipart, parallel)
messages.note: The store checks the signature, not your user session.

messages.label: ObjectCreated v_77/raw.mp4
messages.note: The store emits the event, so nobody polls for finished uploads.

scenarios.name: Alternative: proxy via API
scenarios.summary: Streaming the bytes through your API lets you inspect them on the way in, but every 2 GB upload ties up an API server's bandwidth and a connection for minutes.

messages.label: POST /uploads + 2 GB body
messages.note: The API server holds this connection for the whole transfer.

messages.label: check type, size on the fly
messages.note: The one real advantage: you see every byte before it's stored.

messages.label: PUT bytes (2 GB)
messages.note: Every byte crosses your servers twice, in and out. 100 concurrent uploads means 200 GB of traffic through the API fleet.

messages.label: 201 {video: v_77}
messages.note: Your servers now scale with upload bandwidth, not with requests.

scenarios.name: URL expired
scenarios.summary: The URL is valid for 15 minutes; a client that starts too late gets 403 and asks for a fresh one. That same expiry limits how long a leaked URL is useful.

messages.label: offline for 20 min
messages.note: The phone loses signal before the upload starts.

messages.label: PUT bytes
messages.note: The signature is still correct, but its expiry time has passed.

messages.label: POST /uploads/v_77/url
messages.note: Ask for a new URL for the same key; the pending row doesn't change.

messages.label: new URL (15 min)
messages.note: For multipart, sign each part URL when it's needed, so long uploads never run on a stale one.

scenarios.name: Risk: leaked URL
scenarios.summary: Anyone holding the URL can PUT to that key until it expires. Keep it short, scoped to one key and verb, capped in size, and validate the object after it lands.

messages.label: URL ends up in a shared log
messages.note: A crash report or analytics event captures the full URL with its signature.

messages.label: PUT malware.exe to v_77/raw.mp4
messages.note: The signature is valid, so the store accepts it: it checks the URL, not who sends it.

messages.label: ObjectCreated v_77/raw.mp4
messages.note: Because bytes skip your servers, validation runs on this event: check type, size and scan the file, and delete it if it fails.
